title: Apparently Done
subtitle: 网络信息 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 网络信息（人与社会·科学与技术·网络与信息）
meta: 主题语境：网络信息（人与社会·科学与技术·网络与信息）　|　核心词汇：apparently　|　正文 319 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 apparently 的位置与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: ① Apparently, in 1960 the grandmother left the lamp at the window, and everybody in the courtyard said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning: before the February rains the grandmother had ② apparently left the lamp, and nobody had asked a single question. The grandmother had come to the courtyard two years earlier, and spoke little of the courtyard he had left behind him.

The diary for February 1954 puts it plainer. The lamp was ③ apparently unaware, and the child who kept it had ④ apparently kept it twice before the winter came; nothing in the courtyard was ever done apparently in those days. The child wrote that line himself and read it aloud once every year thereafter.

My uncle, who kept the lamp at the far window, meant something else. He left the lamp ⑤ apparently in public, and nobody in the courtyard doubted it; of all who left it that year, he left it ⑥ apparently before dawn. He was not a man who explained himself, and the courtyard had long since stopped asking him to.

By 1967 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the diary. What the line asked for was that the lamp be kept ⑦ apparently every year, and that whoever did it be ⑧ apparently careful about the whole business. Everybody laughed at the wording, and then did exactly what it said, as they always did. Everybody there knew the work had been done apparently.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1970 she left the lamp ⑨ apparently before dawn when nobody else would, and ⑩ Apparently, she said in 1972, that was the part the courtyard never forgot; the diary still speaks apparently of it. She kept the lamp in the same window for thirty years afterwards, and never once said why; the courtyard never forgot how apparently it had been done.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adv. 显然（句中状语，置于助动词之后／动词之前：had apparently left …，文中第 2、9 题两处）
B. adv. 显然（修饰形容词：apparently unaware）
C. adv. 据说（评注性状语，置于句首：Apparently, …，文中第 1、10 题两处）
D. adv. 据说（修饰过去分词：had apparently kept it）
E. adv. 显然（句末状语：… apparently in public）
F. adv. 显然（句末状语：… apparently before dawn，第 6 处）
G. adv. 据说（被动结构中的中位状语：be kept apparently）
H. adv. 据说（修饰形容词：be apparently careful about the whole business）

answers.why: apparently 意为“显然”，此处置于句首作评注性状语，修饰整个句子：Apparently, in 1960 …。
apparently 意为“显然”，此处置于助动词与过去分词之间修饰动词：had apparently left the lamp。
apparently 意为“显然”，此处修饰形容词 unaware（未察觉）：was apparently unaware。
apparently 意为“据说”，此处修饰过去分词 kept：had apparently kept it twice。
apparently 意为“显然”，此处置于句末修饰动词：left the lamp apparently in public。
apparently 意为“显然”，此处亦置于句末：of all who did it that 年头, he did it apparently before dawn。
apparently 意为“据说”，被动结构 be kept apparently 中，副词置于过去分词之后。
apparently 意为“据说”，此处修饰形容词 careful（仔细）：be apparently careful about the whole business。
apparently 意为“显然”，1970 年母亲在无人肯做时又一次离开那件小小的灯，副词置于动词之后。
apparently 意为“据说”，母亲 1972 年那句话以评注性状语开头：Apparently, …，修饰整句。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1960 年，祖母据说在窗边离开那件小小的灯；院子里人人都说那是头一回。（Apparently, …）
雨季到来之前，祖母已经显然离开那件小小的灯。（had apparently left …）
那件小小的灯当时显然未察觉。（apparently unaware）
保管它的那位孩子在入冬前已经据说把它守着过两回。（had apparently kept it）
叔叔显然离开那件小小的灯，院子里没有一个人怀疑。（… apparently …）
在那个年头里做过这件事的人当中，他做得最显然。（the most apparently of all of them）
answers: Apparently, in 1960 the grandmother left the lamp at the window.
Before the February rains the grandmother had apparently left the lamp.
The child who kept it had apparently kept it twice before the winter came.
He left the lamp apparently in public, and nobody in the courtyard doubted it.
Of all who did it that year, he did it apparently before dawn.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 apparently 的 3 种不同位置（句首评注、句中、句末、被动结构中等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: Apparently, in 1960 the grandmother left the lamp, and nobody forgot it.
Before the February rains the grandmother had apparently left the lamp.
The lamp was apparently unaware, or so the diary says.
The child had apparently kept it twice before the winter came.
My mother left the lamp apparently before dawn when nobody else would.
Apparently, the courtyard never forgot that part of the story.
